### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3fbf3ca6173e80dc515448fd0df497dfb3aed29c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `eb65f705ae7da7b9de4649e9931b515ab32645b5` — the merge of head `8d585eadd1eeae6355cd641d08d54418b6e21576` into base `3fbf3ca6173e80dc515448fd0df497dfb3aed29c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin eb65f705ae7da7b9de4649e9931b515ab32645b5 && git checkout eb65f705ae7da7b9de4649e9931b515ab32645b5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3fbf3ca6173e80dc515448fd0df497dfb3aed29c 8d585eadd1eeae6355cd641d08d54418b6e21576 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3fbf3ca6173e80dc515448fd0df497dfb3aed29c && git merge --no-ff 8d585eadd1eeae6355cd641d08d54418b6e21576

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3fbf3ca6173e80dc515448fd0df497dfb3aed29c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8d585eadd1eeae6355cd641d08d54418b6e21576`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #20859 (body and its six comments: triage 5912813886, release 5913765727, claim 5918346956, `os-dev-report` 5920005720, seat answer 5920030329, delta report 5920225694); PR #20944 body, file list and the net diff against `main` at the head (3 files, +289/-4: `.changeset/20859-cube-filter-array-lowered.md`, `packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-analytics.ts`, `packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-analytics-filter-array-where.test.ts`); precedent PR #20857 (#20810, `793fb839`) and its two changesets; the head's check-runs. The head was still `8d585eadd1` when read (one changeset-only commit on `ca8448c005`; the merge base with `main` is `67c1b11a20`).

Check-runs on the head, read once at 2026-09-30T21:53Z and not polled: 40 runs, none failed. In progress at that moment: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core (1/6)`, `Test Core (4/6)`. Success: `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` and its three shards, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test Core (2/6, 3/6, 5/6, 6/6)`, the four `Type Check ·` lanes (`workspace`, `source gates`, `consumer gates`, `debt ledger`), `Check Changeset` (both runs), `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the claim, single-writer and part-of guards, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `filter`. Skipped: `Console Pin Gate`, `Build Docs`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, one `Auto Label` and one `Check PR Size` run. The commit status `Vercel` is pending. Of the seven required contexts, four are green and three were still running when read; nothing is red. No governed surface is in the file list.

### ① Derived judgments

Read against the spec pair (`packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts`: `isFilterAST`, `parseFilterAST`, `VALID_AST_OPERATORS`), the analytics `where` door (`packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/filter-normalizer.ts`: `lowerAnalyticsWhere`, `filterArrayNotLowerableError`) and the engine door (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`: `lowerWhereFilterArray`), all at the head.

1. **The lowering is the same one, with no second parser — RIGHT.** `lowerWhereFilterArray` in `memory-analytics.ts` gives the three arrival answers `lowerAnalyticsWhere` and the engine door give, in the same order: `[]` is no filter; `isFilterAST` gates before `parseFilterAST` (so the lenient `$op` fallback in `convertComparison` is never reached by an unknown operator); anything else array-shaped is refused. The function contains no parsing logic of its own; the operator list in its message is derived from `VALID_AST_OPERATORS`, the set the spec derives from its one operator table. The "unreachable" branch is unreachable by construction (an array `isFilterAST` accepts lowers, by induction over the three node shapes, to a non-empty object), and it is kept loud exactly as the other two doors keep theirs.
2. **`[]` still means no filter — RIGHT.** It returns `undefined`, the object branch is skipped, and `normalizeFilters` returns an empty list: no `$match` stage and no `WHERE`. At the base an array of any length skipped the branch, so the `[]` answer is unchanged, and it is the reading `parseFilterAST([])` and both other doors give.
3. **Both exits read the lowered list — RIGHT.** `query()` and `generateSql()` each call `this.normalizeFilters(query)`, and the lowering sits at that method's entry; the reassigned `where` is the only read of `query.where` in the file.
4. **No path still drops an array silently — RIGHT.** Every array is one of: empty (no filter, by contract), lowered and handed to the step-3 door, or thrown. The object branch's `!Array.isArray(where)` test is therefore always true for what reaches it, as the acceptance note says. A non-array `where` is untouched by this diff: an object meets the step-3 door as before; `undefined` / `null` is no filter. (A scalar `where` such as a string is still read as no filter — pre-existing, outside this card, and the same reading `lowerAnalyticsWhere` gives a non-object `where`; noted, not filed here.)
5. **The refusal row — RIGHT: same envelope and same shapes as the analytics door.** The face refuses through `unsupportedFilterError` (`filter-refusal.ts`: `code` `INVALID_FILTER`, `status` 400), the analytics door through `invalidFilterError` (same code, same status), and all three doors gate on the same `isFilterAST`, so the refused set is identical by construction. The message renders through `previewFilterArray`, which wraps `JSON.stringify` in try/catch and falls back to `String(value)` or a kind word, so a `bigint` element, `undefined`, or a cyclic value cannot turn the refusal into a raw `TypeError`. The lowerable-but-refused arrays are refused where their object spelling is: a scalar `in` comparand and an `undefined` comparand by the shared shape and type faces inside `parseFilterAST` (`INVALID_FILTER` / 400 from the spec); `starts_with` by this face's own gate (`$startsWith` is not a key of `MONGO_TO_CUBE_OPERATOR`, so `assertFilterConditionShape` refuses it, as #20857 left it).
6. **The two shared comparand faces run twice on an array — RIGHT, and harmless.** `parseFilterAST` runs `assertListComparandShapes` then `normalizeFilterComparandTypes`; the step-3 door runs them again on the returned condition. The first is an assertion, the second is copy-on-write narrowing that is a no-op on its own output, so the second pass cannot move a verdict.
7. **Public surface — unchanged, RIGHT.** No export, type or schema moves; the three new functions are module-private; the added imports come from `@objectstack/spec/data`, which `driver-memory` already depends on (`workspace:*`) and whose barrel re-exports `filter.zod` wholesale. No new dependency edge, no spec artefact to regenerate.
8. **Pins — RIGHT as written.** The file carries 16 cases (the card's row, seven spellings each paired with the object it lowers to, the `[]` control, four non-lowerable arrays refused on both exits, three lowerable arrays refused as their object spelling is); refusals assert `code` + `status` only; the echo control is the one the card asked for; the file imports `./memory-analytics.js` relatively while `vitest.config.ts` aliases every `@objectstack/spec/*` namespace to `spec/src/*/index.ts`, so the ablation sentence "no build sat between the mutation and the reading" is true. The ablation's restored blob `cc0aaa764022` is the head's blob of `memory-analytics.ts`. The run counts (15/1 red, 16/16 green, 66 files / 1429 passed) are the dev's readings and were not re-run here; 66 test files exist under `driver-memory` at the head, and the Test Core shards are the gate.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset:** `@objectstack/driver-memory` (published: `publishConfig.access: public`, no `private` flag) at `minor`, carrying `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, a `**BREAKING**` paragraph, the migration line, and one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` inside an HTML comment. The PR body's line 2 carries the same `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. Under `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` a declared `(narrowing)` is BREAKING and ships `minor` in the launch window; `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- **The grade, judged on the diff — RIGHT.** The widening question is truthfully `no`: no new key lands on a published payload, and a lowerable array was already accepted (answered, wrongly) before, so its corrected answer widens nothing. The narrowing arm is real: on a published export, a non-lowerable array `where` that used to be answered (every row) is now refused, and a lowerable array whose condition the doors refuse is now refused. That the declared schema never admitted those arrays does not change the face's measured accept set, and the precedent on this same face (#20857: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `minor`, BREAKING, the same marker) graded the identical situation — comparands the schema never admitted — as a narrowing; grading this `no` would give one face two readings. The precedent's `yes` came from its widenings (`$or`, `$null`, `$between`); this diff has none, so `no (narrowing)` is the right arm. The first round's `patch` / bare `no` was wrong for the same reason, and the regrade commit touches the changeset alone.
- **The marker's stated facts, each judged:** nothing authorable changes spelling or type — true (no spec key, export or stored row moves). `AnalyticsQuerySchema.where` is `FilterConditionSchema.optional()` (`analytics.zod.ts`), a `z.record(...)` intersected with a `z.object(...)`, neither of which admits an array — true, it never admitted the refused shapes; `FilterArraySchema` (a union of comparison tuple, logic group and non-empty list) admits none of the four either. The analytics door and the engine already refuse the same shapes with the same envelope — true. The package publishes — true. No ADR-0087 conversion covers a runtime filter-shape refusal, and the change is runtime behaviour rather than a declaration — consistent with the precedent's identical marker on this face. The gate's one mechanical check for this category (no migration prescription in the body) reads the same remedy-sentence shape the precedent shipped; the dev's `check:adr-0087-registration` run reported exit 0, and CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` was still running when read.
- **The BREAKING paragraph's list — complete and true.** The first class, "a `where` array that is not a filter — one `isFilterAST` rejects", is the exact complement of the lowered set, so it is complete by construction; each of the four examples fails `isFilterAST` for the stated reason (an infix join's first element is neither a keyword nor a field, and not every element is a node; `sounds_like` is outside `VALID_AST_OPERATORS`; a scalar list has no node; a cube-style entry list has object elements). The second class, "an array that does lower but carries a comparand or operator the face refuses in its object spelling", covers every remaining newly refused arrival, including the pin file's `undefined`-comparand row; both named examples are true (point 5 above). "It too used to answer every row" is true at the base for any array. `[]` unchanged: true.
- **The review faces, sentence by sentence:** every factual sentence of the changeset and of the PR body ("What changed", the three-answer table, "Measured", "Tests", "Acceptance notes") is true against the head and the code named above, including the two the seat edited after the regrade (line 2, and the accept-set bullet's last sentence, which now states the seat's answer and the changeset's shape). The measured counts (run totals, 60 gate families, and the base blob `d78a0bda07`, which is an ancestor of the head) are the dev's readings; nothing in the artefacts contradicts them. No sentence found false.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **The stop clause not stopped on — answered, accepted.** The order (claim 5918346956) says the array spelling is never dropped, and the card's scope says it is lowered or refused loudly and never dropped. For an array `isFilterAST` rejects there is no lowering, so the refusal is the only order-compliant answer and the alternative is the forbidden one. The dev implemented it, named it in the report's summary, deviations and `open_questions`, and the seat answered the grade (B). The code did not move on the regrade; only the changeset did.
2. **Behind `main` — answered, with an update.** When the first report was written, `main` was at `bee75cebe6`, three commits past the merged `67c1b11a20`, and none of the three touches `driver-memory`, `spec/src/data` or `core/src` — true as written. As of this read, `main` is eight commits past the merge base, and two of the later five do touch the named directories: #20924 (`3fbf3ca617`) edits `driver-memory/src/filter-refusal.ts` (message prose only; `unsupportedFilterError`, the helper this diff calls, is byte-identical on both sides) and `core/src/*`; #20934 (`31c39964fc`) edits `spec/src/data/field.form.ts`. Neither touches `memory-analytics.ts`, `filter.zod.ts` or the new pin; the diff's added lines carry no tracker number (the thing #20924 stripped); GitHub reports the PR mergeable; the delta report itself recorded the stale-tree notice. The queue rebuilds on current `main`, which is the re-verification this needs. No re-merge is owed for this record.
3. **The out-of-scope note — verified, escalated to the seat.** `filterArrayNotLowerableError` in the analytics door and the engine door's `!isFilterAST` refusal both interpolate a bare `JSON.stringify(where)`, which throws a `TypeError` on a `bigint` element, so an in-process caller sending a non-lowerable array holding a `bigint` would get a raw throw instead of the envelope. No JSON wire can carry one, so "carrier: none" is right for the wire; both services are published exports, so an in-process reach exists. The facts are correct and the note is in the shape Prime Directive #10 asks for; whether it is filed is the seat's call, not this record's.
4. **The rate-limit stop and resume — answered.** The branch carries exactly the commits the narrative names, each with the file set it claims: `62eff2a8f9` (the pin file alone), `f2be8432cd` (`memory-analytics.ts` alone), `0d27cf3465` (the changeset), `ca8448c005` (the merge of `67c1b11a20`), `8d585eadd1` (the changeset regrade alone). Nothing was redone and nothing is missing.
5. **`open_questions[0]` (keep `no`, or take `(narrowing)`) — answered B by the seat; judged B on the diff in ② above.**
